newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Bookover halves Terexko after cautionary.
newsitem.headline: Bookover halves Terexko after cautionary.

text.p: In the wake of a cautionary announcement earlier shares in South African conference to hotels company Terexko Ltd hacked off more than half their value in a single bookover trade.
Dealers said that, while the company's announcement it was considering certain sub judice matters had been taken as negative, the cautionary was insufficient to punish the share price this much.
The share cut 148 cents to 102 cents with 2,000 shares changing hands. It was last at 122.00/220.00 cents.

"It was a bookover and was both bought and sold by the same buyer at 102 cents. The cautionary is bad, but it's not that bad. It's more than likely a case of willing buyer, willing seller," one dealer said.
Dealers said that there was also the possibility the number may have been incorrectly entered as it was unlikely the broker would have bought and sold as low as 102 cents.
But they said that even if the broker had traded at the 102 cents level he made neither loss or gain because of the nature of the bookover deal.
